quality_assessment: Chapter is well-written and accurate with minor missing details. Content correctly documents all sorting modes and their performance implications. Primarily needs to mention the deprecated --sort-files flag and the explicit --sort=none option.

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention the deprecated --sort-files flag
issues.should_add: Document that --sort-files is deprecated and users should use --sort=path instead
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a note in 'Sort Options' or a new 'Deprecated Options' section mentioning --sort-files is deprecated in favor of --sort=path. This helps users migrating from older ripgrep versions.

issues.description: Chapter shows --sort none in example but doesn't explicitly document it as an option
issues.current_content:
# No sorting (default, fastest)
rg --sort none pattern
issues.should_be: More explicitly document that --sort=none is available to override config files or previous --sort flags
issues.fix_suggestion: Add explicit documentation that --sort=none can be used to explicitly disable sorting, which is useful for overriding configuration files or previous command-line flags

issues.description: Chapter mentions platform differences but doesn't explain error behavior when timestamps unavailable
issues.should_add: Explain that ripgrep will detect unavailable timestamps, print an error, and exit without searching
issues.fix_suggestion: Add to 'Sorting Across Platforms' section: When a requested sort criterion is unavailable on the filesystem (e.g., creation time on ext4), ripgrep detects this, prints an error message, and exits without performing the search.

issues.description: Performance comparison provides specific numbers that appear to be estimates rather than actual benchmarks
issues.current_content:
For large codebases:
- Unsorted: ~100ms
- Sorted by path: ~500ms
- Sorted by time: ~600ms
issues.should_be: Either provide actual benchmark methodology or make it clearer these are example/approximate values
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify these are approximate example values, not benchmarks from a specific system. Consider adding 'Example:' prefix or note that actual values depend on hardware, file count, and filesystem.

positive_aspects: Clear explanation of all four sort modes (path, modified, accessed, created)
Correctly documents that sorting disables parallelism
Good progression from simple examples to complex use cases
Performance impact well explained with practical implications
Excellent 'When Not to Sort' section with clear guidance
Practical examples showing real-world use cases
Best practices section provides actionable advice
Good integration with other features (context, file types, JSON output)
improvement_suggestions: Add brief mention of deprecated --sort-files flag for legacy users
Explicitly document --sort=none as a way to override config files
Explain error behavior when timestamps are unavailable
Clarify that performance numbers are examples, not benchmarks
Consider adding example of using --sort=none to override config file setting
Could add note about --no-sort-files negation flag for completeness

metadata.validation_focus: Verify sorting options and their impact on performance are documented
metadata.validation_result: PASSED - Sorting options and performance impact are well documented with minor omissions
